references.text: The description of the ephod made for the high priest, with gold and precious stones. Gideon's ephod was likely inspired by this holy object.
Israel is described as committing spiritual adultery by following other gods. The same language is used regarding Israel's relationship to Gideon's ephod.
The warning that idols will become a snare for Israel. Gideon's ephod became just such a snare for him and his household.
Mica made an ephod and household gods, and appointed his own priest. Similar unauthorized religious practice as with Gideon's ephod.
The ephod and other cult objects from Mica's house were stolen by the tribe of Dan. Shows how such objects led to idolatry.
The psalmist describes how Israel's idolatry became a snare for them, using the same wording as in Judges 8:27.
Hosea prophesies that Israel will be without an ephod for many days. Refers to the role of the ephod in Israel's religious life.
